claims: A reduced-cost certificate with margin epsilon remains valid after edge weights are perturbed downward by at most epsilon.
Margin absorption composes with the arbitrage certificate theorem to prove no-arbitrage cycles for perturbed actual weights.
A conservative k-hop rounding budget of 2*k-1 can be used as the required certificate margin.
Under a Lipschitz-1 rounding model, the tighter k-hop margin k is sufficient.
A margin sized for k hops also covers any smaller j-hop perturbation budget when j <= k.
Concrete witnesses show sufficient margin, insufficient margin, and exact-threshold tightness.
proof_method: integer linear arithmetic for margin absorption
monotonicity of the conservative hop budget
explicit finite witnesses for survival, failure, and tightness
